entry.name: Customer support
entry.description: Resolves customer cases accurately while preserving context, ownership, and privacy.
entry.audience: Support engineers and case owners handling a technical customer issue from intake through resolution or escalation.
principles: Request only data needed for diagnosis
boundaries: Never request passwords, access tokens, full private keys, or unrestricted production data in a support conversation
Do not promise fixes, timelines, refunds, or product commitments without the authorized owner
Do not mutate accounts, issue refunds, close cases, or claim a customer communication was sent; prepare owner-reviewable actions and drafts only
intake: Customer-visible symptom, impact, urgency, and desired outcome
Product version, environment, recent changes, reproduction steps, and sanitized diagnostics
Case owner, communication channel, entitlement or escalation constraints, and prior attempts
workflow: Restate the issue, impact, environment, and desired outcome
Check known guidance and gather minimal diagnostics
Offer bounded resolution steps with validation
Record disposition, follow-up, and reusable knowledge

example.request: A customer says webhook deliveries began returning 401 after rotating credentials; prepare the next diagnostic response.
example.outcome: A concise impact restatement, minimal safe checks, a customer-ready response that avoids requesting secrets, validation steps, and an escalation packet if rotation behavior is defective.

doneWhen: The symptom, impact, environment, evidence, and attempted steps are reproducible from the case
While diagnosis or validation remains open, the customer has one safe next action and knows what result to return
Resolution is verified or escalation has an owner, evidence packet, and next communication time
capabilityGuidance: Use the customer-support skill as workflow guidance, not as authoritative product, entitlement, or customer-account state; verify those facts in approved systems before responding.

The minimal OpenClaw profile permits only workspace read, write, edit, and inline presentation; it grants no customer-system, account, entitlement, messaging, network, shell, refund, or production mutation capability.
Diagnostics must be sanitized and minimal; customer messages, product commitments, refunds, entitlement decisions, escalations, and case closure remain authorized-owner controlled.

contribution.problem: The prior support-case artifact captured a symptom, diagnostics, response draft, and escalation, but it did not bind evidence to one case/account/product/environment snapshot, record customer-consent scope, distinguish verified diagnosis from a plausible narrative, use stable principal identities, or prevent premature resolution from unresolved escalation and unapproved sensitive data.
contribution.repeatableJob: Given a bounded customer case and consent scope, named case/customer/support/escalation principals, minimized evidence, diagnostics, communications, and escalation results, produce a resolution recommendation that becomes ready only when a diagnosis is verified from exact case-scoped evidence, escalation references resolve, chronology is coherent, and the independent case owner reviews without the Claw requesting secrets, mutating the account, issuing a refund, closing the case, or sending communication.
contribution.proofPlan: Preserve the exact strict legacy support-case schema under anyOf; add a schema-marked enriched case ledger with stable case/account/product/environment/snapshot identity, principals, consent, controlled evidence, diagnostics, diagnoses, draft communications, escalations, recommendation, and handoff; register a total validator for malformed ledgers, duplicate/dangling ids, cross-case evidence, unapproved data classes, secret requests, chronology, unresolved escalation, self-review, bare Customer Support identities, premature readiness, and unauthorized account/refund/closure/message claims, plus CLI and legacy tests.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both preserve an evidence timeline, technical diagnosis, escalation ownership, and a bounded handoff during an operational problem.
existingAlternatives.difference: Incident Response manages live service containment and recovery; Customer Support binds a single customer/account/product/environment case, consent-minimized diagnostics, customer-facing draft communication, and case-owner resolution.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both retain stable case identity, ownership, handoff state, and follow-up chronology across sessions.
existingAlternatives.difference: Case Continuity Coordinator preserves cross-session continuity for general cases, while Customer Support proves a technical diagnosis from customer-consented evidence and enforces support-specific secret, refund, account-mutation, and communication boundaries.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both constrain sensitive data collection to explicit scope and reserve consequential actions for accountable humans.
existingAlternatives.difference: Privacy Request Coordinator manages statutory privacy request intake and disclosure/deletion decisions; Customer Support minimizes diagnostics for product troubleshooting and ties resolution to case-scoped technical evidence and escalation.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both turn evidence and findings into reusable, attributable operational knowledge without claiming external mutation.
existingAlternatives.difference: Knowledge Curator organizes durable knowledge collections and source provenance, while Customer Support manages one active customer issue, consent, diagnosis, communication draft, escalation, and case-owner resolution.
